script.voiceText: [deep, cinematic documentary narrator, calm authority, crisp pace] Put these on... and the roar of the engines fades away. [playful, curious, quick] How? They fight sound... with MORE sound. Sound is a pressure wave: squeeze, stretch, squeeze, stretch. Tiny microphones on the ear cups listen to the noise outside. A chip builds the exact opposite wave. The speaker plays it. Where a peak meets a trough... they cancel. Wave plus anti-wave equals... almost silence! It works best on low, steady hums. The cushions block higher sounds. And engineers built an electronic sound absorber back in nineteen fifty-three! Your quiet is made of noise... turned upside down.

claims.claim: Active noise control: a microphone senses the noise and a loudspeaker produces a cancelling signal; the first electronic sound absorber was built in 1953.
claims.source: Olson & May (1953), Electronic sound absorber, J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 25:1130-1136; Leventhall, Active attenuators: a historical review (Institute of Acoustics)

claims.claim: Cancellation works by destructive interference of an inverted (anti-phase) wave and is most effective at low frequencies; passive isolation handles higher frequencies.
claims.source: Shi, Lam & Gan (2023), Active Noise Control in the New Century: The Role and Prospect of Signal Processing (review)
